reasoning_steps: Step 1: Set up the geometric configuration: A point charge +Q is situated at the center of the square base of a right pyramid with four identical sloped triangular faces.

Step 2: Method 1 (Symmetric Bipyramid Construction): Construct an identical inverted square pyramid below the base, joined base-to-base. The resulting 8-faced polyhedron (a square bipyramid / octahedron) completely encloses the charge +Q at its exact center of symmetry.
Step 3: Apply Gauss's Law: The total electric flux emerging through the closed surface of the 8-faced bipyramid is Phi_total = Q / epsilon_0.

Step 4: Invoke symmetry: By the full point group symmetry (D_4h) of the bipyramid, all 8 triangular faces are geometrically identical and symmetrically disposed with respect to the central charge +Q. Therefore, the flux is equally partitioned among the 8 faces.
Step 5: Compute flux per face: Phi_face = Phi_total / 8 = Q / (8 * epsilon_0).

Step 6: Method 2 (Half-Space Flux Check): The charge lies on the plane of the base (z = 0). The electric field lines in the z = 0 plane are tangential to the base, so the flux through the flat base is zero. Exactly half of the spherical field lines pass into the upper hemisphere (z > 0), giving a total upward flux of Q / (2 * epsilon_0). By the 4-fold rotational symmetry about the pyramid's axis, this upward flux is equally distributed among the 4 upper triangular faces, yielding (1/4) * (Q / (2 * epsilon_0)) = Q / (8 * epsilon_0).
Step 7: Both methods conclude that the flux through one upper face is Q / (8 * epsilon_0), which corresponds to Option C.
assumptions_used: The pyramid is a right pyramid with a square base and four congruent triangular upper faces
The medium is vacuum/air with permittivity epsilon_0
The point charge is located precisely at the center of the square base
diagram_interpretation: 3D perspective of a right square pyramid with charge +Q centered on the square base and four sloped triangular faces converging at the apex.
